title: Double bets explained: doubles, each-way doubles and two singles

scenes.say: A double is one bet on two selections, and both have to win. It's the smallest accumulator, and the each-way version is two bets, not one.
scenes.caption: A double is one bet on two selections, and both have to win. It's the smallest accumulator, and the each-way version is two bets, not one.

visual.title: Two selections, one bet, both must win

scenes.say: Here's five pounds on a six to four and a two to one: the return from the first rides on the second. Five, times two and a half, times three, is thirty-seven pounds fifty.
scenes.caption: Here's £5 on a 6/4 and a 2/1: the return from the first rides on the second. £5 × 2.50 × 3.00 = £37.50.

scenes.say: The same five pounds as two singles of two pounds fifty would return thirteen pounds seventy-five if both won. But if only one wins, the singles still pay something. The double pays nothing.
scenes.caption: The same £5 as two singles of £2.50 would return £13.75 if both won. But if only one wins, the singles still pay something. The double pays nothing.

scenes.say: Each way, it's a win double and a place double: five pounds each way costs ten. At a fifth of the odds, both placed returns nine pounds ten, less than you paid. At eight to one and ten to one, the same result returns thirty-nine pounds.
scenes.caption: Each way, it's a win double and a place double: £5 each way costs £10. At a fifth of the odds, both placed returns £9.10, less than you paid. At 8/1 and 10/1, the same result returns £39.

scenes.say: If one selection is a non-runner, it usually counts at odds of one, so the double becomes a single on the other: twelve pounds fifty. Some boosted multiples are voided instead, so check the rules where you bet.
scenes.caption: If one selection is a non-runner, it usually counts at odds of 1.0, so the double becomes a single on the other: £12.50. Some boosted multiples are voided instead, so check the rules where you bet.
